newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes end firmer, consolidating diffs weaker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes end firmer, consolidating diffs weaker.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes bumped higher to the close Wednesday, turning early losses to sustained gains on concerns over new cold weather forecasts.
Traders said the market was spooked upon the release of new weather predictions calling for a second blast of Arctic air for the Midwest and Northeast sections of the U.S.
Outright price rallying brought cash February West Texas Intermediate/Cushing to close at $26.55-65 a barrel, 35 cents higher than the ending price seen Tuesday.
Domestic grades remained rangebound at the weaker price differentials established in recent sessions, traders said.
